purpose: ASVS V3.7.3 had no decision. It asks that the application show a notice, with a way to cancel, before taking someone to a URL outside its control. The assistant cites sources it chose and ai-assistant-stream.contract.ts requires every citation uri to match ^https?:// , so each one is absolute by construction. Two surfaces rendered them and both navigated on the click: GektaSourceList in a new tab, AiAssistantPanel in the same tab. Neither asked.
requiredInvariants: It is applicable, and that was established rather than assumed. A survey found no hard-coded external href anywhere in the UI, which would have made this NOT_APPLICABLE; the outbound surface is the assistant's citations, whose absoluteness is guaranteed by the stream contract, not by chance.

The second surface was found before claiming PASS. AiAssistantPanel renders the same citations in the same tab without target=_blank; a guard written only around new tabs would have passed while that path stayed unannounced.
Outbound is decided by comparing origins, the line the browser itself draws, rather than against a list of hosts that would drift from the deployment.
Schemes other than http(s) are refused outright rather than confirmed and then opened, so javascript:, data: and blob: never reach a notice.

The host is shown exactly as the browser resolved it, punycode included. A decoded homograph reads like the site it imitates; the ASCII form is the one that tells a person something true. An earlier draft of that function pretended to decode and then returned the input unchanged - inert code dressed as a feature - and was replaced with what it actually does, said plainly.

Checked and deliberately not changed: the same components render citation.href, which comes from a fixed catalogue of /platform-v7 paths and is same-origin. The guard keys on the contract-absolute field name rather than on anything called a citation, so an internal Next Link is not pushed through an external-link component and does not lose client-side navigation for nothing.

The guard counts the confirmed component itself. An earlier version stopped seeing it once the notice moved into a shared component, so a regression would have read as clean; it now reports 2 confirmed and would report them as unannounced if the component were replaced by a raw anchor.

Revocability is proven at the behaviour, not at the source text: the component tests render, click, cancel and confirm, and assert that the click was defaultPrevented and that window.open was not called.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation. No registration business logic, 1C or marketing change; the presentation change is the security notice this requirement asks for and nothing else.
acceptance: node scripts/security/verify-outbound-navigation-notice.mjs exits 0: 10 anchors needing a notice, 8 literal same-origin, 2 confirmed, 0 unannounced.
vitest run gektaOutboundNavigation.spec.tsx gektaOutboundNotice.spec.ts gektaStandaloneExperience.test.ts: 22 passed, 0 failed.
ASVS V3.7.3 moves NOT_ASSESSED to PASS: PASS 129 to 130, NOT_ASSESSED 39 to 38, FAIL and NOT_APPLICABLE unchanged, rejected decisions back to the single pre-existing V8.2.4.
Seven negative mutations each fail a named test or make the guard exit 1, including removing the marker from the real component.

Full apps/web vitest run: 224 failed files / 373 failed tests / 5211 passed, against a main baseline of 224 / 373 / 5199 - the baseline plus exactly the 12 new tests, with no failing file moved in either direction.
